title: Storytelling
idea: "RYZE ad 1" (Briefs for HS, Brief #16). 1:1 of a Ryze mushroom coffee emotional song ad (1:57, shared as a top performer: "emotional singing ads are the cheat code"): "I felt invisible next to my sister / puffy, bloated and heavy every day", her sister shares her secret, the glow-up. Same song, story and shots; the secret is our castor oil roll-on + belly wrap (her sister's nightly routine) instead of a morning coffee. Bloating backed by our #294, #303, #305; mechanism = Johnny's castor oil pack explanation cut to the reference's length.

script.script:
H1 (ONE hook), sung: I felt invisible next to my sister. Puffy, bloated and heavy every day.
Once H1 is finished, the editor makes 2 more hooks (H2, H3) based on it (see editing notes).
script.visual:
INITIAL IMAGE
H1 (the reference's own first frame, ref 0:00): the two sisters side by side, her sister glamorous in a silk slip dress, her in a dark frumpy dress, hands clasped, looking down.
THEN, LINE BY LINE:
"I felt invisible" → the two sisters side by side (ref 0:00).
"next to my sister" → the party, everyone turned toward her sister, her standing alone in the background (ref 0:03).
"Puffy, bloated and heavy every day" → her pressing a tissue under her puffy eyes at the mirror (ref 0:06).
script.on_screen_text: No header. Captions like the reference.

script.script: I tried everything to feel better. But it all felt like a waste. Spending hours at the gym, eating less and less. Meanwhile she did whatever she wanted, and looked good in every dress.
script.visual:
"I tried everything to feel better" → a kitchen counter covered in supplement bottles and spilled pills (ref 0:09).
"But it all felt like a waste" → her rubbing her tired eyes at the counter (ref 0:12).
"Spending hours at the gym" → her on a treadmill, sweating (ref 0:15).
"eating less and less" → her poking at a tiny salad (ref 0:18).
"Meanwhile she did whatever she wanted" → her sister twirling in a red dress, laughing (ref 0:21).
"and looked good in every dress" → her hugging her knees on the bed, watching (ref 0:24).

script.script: So I finally asked if she could help me. I wanted to be more like her. Feeling snatched, light and free.
script.visual:
"So I finally asked if she could help me" → close-up of her face, vulnerable, turning to her sister (ref 0:27).
"I wanted to be more like her" → the party again, her sister glowing in the crowd (ref 0:30).
"Feeling snatched, light and free" → a dreamy shot of herself glowing in a wine-red dress at the party (ref 0:33).

script.script: She showed me the little amber bottle from her nightly routine. Turns out what helped her glow up was this castor oil. Cold-pressed, rolled on her belly, wrapped up warm while she slept. It soaks in deep to help her let go of the stress. Helped her feel more regular and less puffy. Less of a hot mess.
script.visual:
"She showed me the little amber bottle from her nightly routine" → the sister in the kitchen handing her OUR amber roll-on (ref 0:36-0:39, in place of the cup).
"Turns out what helped her glow up" → OUR roll-on and the cotton wrap on the kitchen counter in warm light (ref 0:42, in place of the bag).
"was this castor oil" → close-up of our label, the bottle glowing (ref 0:45).
"Cold-pressed, rolled on her belly, wrapped up warm while she slept" → close-up of the rose quartz ball rolling golden oil over a belly, then the wrap pulled snug (ref 0:48, their spoon-in-coffee macro).
"It soaks in deep to help her let go of the stress" → 3D shot of golden oil sinking through belly skin, the swollen tissue relaxing.
"Helped her feel more regular and less puffy" → the sister walking in the hallway in green pajamas, light and happy (ref 0:51).
"Less of a hot mess" → the sister smiling at herself in the mirror (ref 0:54).

script.script: So I started wrapping up every single day. And what happened next blew me away.
script.visual:
"So I started wrapping up every single day" → OUR roll-on next to the folded wrap on the nightstand, her hand picking it up (ref 0:57).
"And what happened next blew me away" → her rolling it on her belly and wrapping up, eyes closed (ref 1:00).

script.script: After my first night I didn't feel much. I could feel things start to move in my gut. Within a few days I was going to the bathroom, and not complaining. I was feeling lighter than ever before. Within a few weeks I looked in the mirror and smiled. The puffy, bloated feeling was finally going away. I felt more and more confident every single day.
script.visual:
"After my first night I didn't feel much" → her in pajamas, hand on her belly, unsure (ref 1:03).
"I could feel things start to move in my gut" → a warm glow moving inside her belly under her hand (ref 1:06).
"Within a few days I was going to the bathroom, and not complaining" → her with a finger to her lips, cheeky smile (ref 1:09).
"I was feeling lighter than ever before" → her in jeans and a white tee in the bedroom, jaw dropped, then jumping with her arms up (ref 1:12-1:15).
"Within a few weeks I looked in the mirror and smiled" → close-up of her face, softer, glowing (ref 1:18).
"The puffy, bloated feeling was finally going away" → her in a green dress in the mirror, her sister proud behind her (ref 1:21).
"I felt more and more confident every single day" → the two sisters walking out together, laughing (ref 1:24-1:27).

script.script: The best part is that it's actually so easy. Roll it on, wrap it up and drift off to sleep.
script.visual:
"The best part is that it's actually so easy" → macro of the rose quartz ball rolling golden oil (ref 1:30, their latte froth macro).
"Roll it on, wrap it up and drift off to sleep" → her in bed with the wrap on, eyes closed, smiling (ref 1:33-1:36, their sipping shots).

script.script: It's half off right now, so we both stocked up to keep us on the right track. You can try it risk-free for 30 days, and if you don't love it, you'll get every penny back.
script.visual:
"It's half off right now" → the two sisters at the counter with a stack of our bottles (ref 1:39).
"so we both stocked up to keep us on the right track" → a row of our amber bottles and wraps on the counter (ref 1:42).
"You can try it risk-free for 30 days" → a laptop on the counter showing our product page (ref 1:45).
"and if you don't love it, you'll get every penny back" → the two sisters smiling at each other, our bottles beside them (ref 1:48-1:54).

editing_notes:
Replicate this format exactly: Reference (link above: the video in the X post; it's a Ryze mushroom coffee song ad, 1:57). SAME SONG, SAME STORY, SAME SHOTS. Only swaps: the product is our castor oil roll-on + cotton belly wrap (her sister's NIGHT routine instead of a morning cup), and the lyrics about the product. Lyrics follow the reference's syllables and rhymes line for line.
HOOKS: build ONE hook first (H1, the reference's own opening: the sung line "I felt invisible next to my sister. Puffy, bloated and heavy every day" over the reference's first frame, the two sisters side by side). Once H1 is done, make 2 more hooks (H2, H3) based on it: same sung line and same body, each with a new first frame / initial image that shows the same problem just as clearly (e.g. her alone at the mirror pulling at her bloated belly; her sister twirling in a red dress while she watches from the bed). Deliver H1, H2, H3.
ALL CHARACTERS ARE WHITE (Caucasian).
FRAME BY FRAME: every Visual cell goes line by line (lyric → the one shot to show, with the reference timestamp it copies). Same camera, framing, light and timing. Every lyric gets the shot that shows exactly that lyric.
PRODUCT: wherever the reference shows the Ryze bag or a coffee cup (ref 0:39-0:48, 0:57, 1:30-1:45), show OUR amber roll-on + the cotton belly wrap in the same 3D style, built from the real product photos (Products tab).
MUSIC: the same song as the reference (melody, tempo, key, arrangement); only our lyrics change.
CAPTIONS: small white captions centred, a few words at a time, one key word in bold, exactly like the reference.
B-ROLL: Pixar-style 3D animation exactly like the reference (same look, warm light, character style). Only the product changes.
PROOF: Ryze runs this emotional song format right now; bloating angle = our winners #294, #303, #305.
CLAIMS (strong, like the reference): "going to the bathroom and not complaining" and "puffy bloated feeling finally going away" are the strongest.
OFFER (evergreen): half off right now (Buy 3 Get 3 Free) + 30-day money-back guarantee. Landing page: Bloating page.
Doc: Briefs for HS, tab "RYZE ad 1" (Brief #16).

Voiceover: Sung by an AI female vocalist exactly like the reference: same melody, same key, same tempo, same soft emotional pop style, every lyric sung clearly so it's understood on the first listen. It must sound like a real singer, never robotic. NEEDS TO HAVE CONVICTION in their voice, its boring to listen to a dull script. They need to speak with character.

Avatar: Pixar-style 3D characters exactly like the reference. ALL CHARACTERS ARE WHITE (Caucasian): her, her sister and everyone at the party.
HER (the singer/narrator): white woman about 45 to 50, short curly brown hair, kind face; at the start puffy face, bloated belly, frumpy clothes (ref 0:00-0:24); by the end slimmer, glowing, long hair down, fitted green dress (ref 1:21-1:27). Same face throughout.
HER SISTER: white, slim, blonde, glamorous, about 45, effortless (ref 0:00, 0:21, 0:51-0:54).
